To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quality of financial institutions is a source of comparative advantages and that the size of financial market relative to the GDP does not adequately capture this quality.

the financial system is a source of comparative advantages, that financial institutions in developing economies are not necessarily inferior to those in advanced economies, and that financial development may be a source of comparative disadvantage.
Financial institutions are a source of comparative advantages in the South and a source of comparative disadvantages in the North.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of financial system quality in the process of trade and development.
the role of financial institutions in the process of international trade.
the role of the financial sector in the process of international trade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quality of the Financial System is a source of comparative advantages in the South, and the quality of the system in the North is a source of competitive advantage in the South, but not vice versa.
the quality of financial institutions is a source of comparative advantages.
financial institutions are an important determinant of trade flows and the welfare of countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of institutions, not just their size, is an important determinant of comparative advantage in international trade.
financial development is a source of comparative disadvantage in the South.
financial development and financial integration are complementary and mutually reinforcing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
financial institutions can be a source of comparative advantages.
the role of finance in trade and development should be studied in a general equilibrium context.
financial development may be the key to understanding the pattern of international trade.
